model.architecture: Granite 4.1-3B is IBM's 3.4B-parameter dense instruct model (40 layers, hidden 2560, GQA 40:8, tied embeddings, 100k vocab), long-context and tool-calling capable, released April 2026.

variants.quantization: int4 blockwise-32 + OCTAV on linears, int8 embedding

recommended.reason: the Android path measured on a Pixel 8a (Tensor G3): 7.07 tok/s decode on gpu; the same phone's cpu row decodes 6.98 tok/s; the repo's granite-4.1-3b_int8.litertlm decodes 3.86 tok/s on the same device and backend, so this file carries the class

the Android path verified on a Galaxy S26 (S4 gate 2026-08-24): full delegation (12119 ops across 7 subgraphs) and a correct answer to the probe; 16.1 tok/s decode, engine init 14.1 s, peak 1394 MB. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is the verified choice for the class, not a measured win over CPU; the repo's granite-4.1-3b_int8.litertlm decodes 11.18 tok/s on the same device and backend, so this file carries the class

platform_notes: int4 is the file to use on a phone: on Apple hardware it is both smaller and faster than int8.

Six prefill signatures (1024, 256, 64, 16, 4, 1) with a 4096-token KV budget; an eleven-signature build was killed by iOS during Metal init unless context was capped at 1024; this file creates its engine at the full 4096 on iPhone 17 Pro.
int4 carries the trimmed six-signature ladder and is the file to use on iOS.
Pixel 8a: GPU wins prefill (3.7x) and TTFT (3.3x), not decode (7.07 vs 6.98 tok/s); on Apple hardware the GPU wins across the board.
int4 beats int8 on the GPU on both platforms (1.2x decode on Metal, 1.8x on Mali); int8 wins CPU prefill (2.5x on Mac).
A 3.4B model on a mid-range phone is not a fast experience in absolute terms.
Android GPU: XNNPACK takes 1 of 4 nodes in decode_embedder and prefill_embedder_1024; the runtime accepts that split.
Embedder externalised so the tied 100352x2560 vocab table sits in its own section, clear of the ~2 GiB single-section mmap ceiling on iOS.
